overall: Washington, DC is running well below model expectations this morning: the daily maximum of 75.9°F was actually set around midnight (00:12 ET, roughly 7.6 hours ago), and temperatures have been flat or gently declining since, sitting at 73.4°F under a complete overcast (OVC, ceiling just 183m) as of 07:49 ET. A tropical air mass is in place — evidenced by the oppressively high dewpoint of 71.6°F and an active Flood Watch — and this moisture-saturated environment is suppressing solar heating almost entirely, with zero warming velocity recorded.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model disagreement: the synoptic-scale GFS and ECMWF are projecting 84.9°F and 83.7°F respectively, while the mesoscale HRRR and NBM — better suited to capturing convective suppression and cloud cover — come in considerably lower at 81.2°F and 81.3°F. The NWS text forecast of 'near 85°F' aligns with the global models, but current surface observations (flat trend, 100% cloud cover, low ceiling) and the META model's strong 37% concentration in the 78–79°F bucket argue that even the HRRR/NBM may be slightly optimistic.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence — zero warming velocity at 07:49 ET, OVC skies with a ceiling barely above 600 feet, a tropical-moisture-suppressed boundary layer, and the META model's dominant probability at 78–79°F — points to a daily high landing somewhere in the 78–81°F range rather than near the NWS-forecast 85°F. For the active Kalshi odd-bucket market, the top bucket of 83–84°F (30.5%) appears overpriced given current conditions; the 77–82°F odd buckets look more attractive. Best single-point estimate is approximately 79°F, though a late-afternoon storm outflow or brief convective mixing event introduces upside tail risk toward 82°F. Confidence is moderate-low given the tropical/convective uncertainty.
